claim_one_line: THE B500 DEPTH-5 REOPEN ATTEMPTED AND THE METHOD KILLED BY ITS OWN CONTROL -- L145a STAYS OPEN, the attempt failing on the INSTRUMENT not on the object. cc3's sweep surfaced B500 (revival_score 6, the highest in the kill graph, and in NO register), whose own text downgrades its kill to PROVISIONAL with 35 words UNCHECKED (26 timeouts + 9 never-reached, the D/M-heavy tail whose resultant eliminants blow up to degree ~3000-9280 beyond in-sandbox gp), and B525 specifies the reopen as 'F_p Groebner or longer timeout'. THE ROUTE PROPOSED: K = Q[t]/(t^4-t-1) is S4-quartic with NO intermediate fields so the child is present iff the eliminant h has a root in K; if p is INERT then O_K/p = F_{p^4} and a root in K reduces to a root in F_{p^4}, so contrapositively h mod p having NO root in F_{p^4} PROVES h has no root in K -- via gcd(h, x^{p^4}-x) by repeated squaring, cheap even at degree 9280, with the whole resultant chain run in GF(p) so the Q blow-up never happens. WHAT CAME BACK: 9 words computed with eliminant degrees 6450-7896 and a root in F_{p^4} at both inert primes 5 and 19; 26 words DEGENERATE, the resultant chain vanishing identically because they are exactly the words needing hunt_d5.py's SATURATION branch which this script does not implement; ZERO proved absent. THE CONTROL, RUN IMMEDIATELY: at p=5 degree 6500, 28 of 40 RANDOM polynomials have a root in F_{p^4}; at p=19 degree 6500, 29 of 40; at p=5 degree 74, 33 of 40. So about 70 percent of random polynomials PASS, and 'all 9 have a root' is EXACTLY THE BASE RATE, zero information. The LOGIC was correct and the POWER is nil: a degree-6500 polynomial has thousands of roots across small extensions so the informative outcome (NO root) essentially never occurs, and A CRITERION THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A TEST -- MB12 applied to this seat's own instrument. THE GENERALISABLE REASON: any test of the form 'does h have a root of type X' is saturated at these degrees, and a discriminating test must use THE SPECIFIC FIELD K rather than merely its degree, i.e. an irreducible degree-4 factor over Q whose field is isomorphic to K, which is what B500's exact route computes and what the mod-p shortcut cannot reach. WHAT GENUINELY STANDS: (1) a REAL INSTRUMENT GAIN -- the eliminants that overflowed the PARI stack over Q are computable in SECONDS mod p, degrees 6450-7896 obtained where the exact route died, so the bottleneck B500 hit is NOT intrinsic and only the decisive test is; (2) the 26 degenerate words are DIAGNOSED NOT LOST, needing the saturation branch that hunt_d5.py already implements, and B525's 'F_p GROEBNER' is most plausibly exactly this -- Groebner OVER F_p to handle saturation -- rather than the root-existence test attempted here; (3) L145a stays OPEN with a sharper statement of what closing it requires, namely mod-p elimination WITH saturation for the 26 plus a FIELD-SPECIFIC rather than degree-specific decisive test for all 35. BANKED RATHER THAN DISCARDED because the attractive half is already written down and would otherwise be re-proposed: recording that the mod-p route computes the eliminants WITHOUT recording that its decisive test is vacuous would hand a later seat a method that looks like it works -- the same propose-and-refute-in-the-same-file pattern cc3 used hours earlier on its own selector reading.
